passages.text: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
passages.sermon:
Job was a man who suffered greatly.
After his friends saw his pain, they sat with him in silence for seven days and nights.
After this time, Job spoke.
Job opened his mouth.
He cursed the day he was born.
passages.original: אַחֲרֵי־ כֵ֗ן פָּתַ֤ח אִיּוֹב֙ אֶת־ פִּ֔יהוּ וַיְקַלֵּ֖ל אֶת־ יוֹמֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: And this is what he said: “May the day of my birth perish, and the night it was said, ‘A boy is conceived.’
passages.sermon:
Job was a man who suffered greatly.
He spoke after his friends sat with him in silence for seven days and nights.
Job opened his mouth.
He said these words.
He said, “May the day I was born perish.
May the night when they said, ‘A boy is conceived,’ be lost.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ יֹ֣אבַד י֭וֹם אִוָּ֣לֶד בּ֑וֹ וְהַלַּ֥יְלָה אָ֝מַ֗ר הֹ֣רָה גָֽבֶר׃

passages.text: If only that day had turned to darkness! May God above disregard it; may no light shine upon it.
passages.sermon:
Job spoke.
Job suffered greatly.
Job cursed the day of his birth.
He said, "Let that day become darkness."
He asked God above to ignore that day.
He said, "Let no light shine on it."
passages.original: הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֗וּא יְֽהִ֫י חֹ֥שֶׁךְ אַֽל־ יִדְרְשֵׁ֣הוּ אֱל֣וֹהַּ מִמָּ֑עַל וְאַל־ תּוֹפַ֖ע עָלָ֣יו נְהָרָֽה׃

passages.text: May darkness and gloom reclaim it, and a cloud settle over it; may the blackness of the day overwhelm it.
passages.sermon:
Job spoke these words.
Job was a man who suffered greatly.
He wished for the day of his birth to be forgotten.
He said, "Let darkness take back that day."
He said, "Let deep shadow cover it."
He said, "Let a cloud rest over it."
He said, "Let the darkness of the day terrify it."
passages.original: יִגְאָלֻ֡הוּ חֹ֣שֶׁךְ וְ֭צַלְמָוֶת תִּשְׁכָּן־ עָלָ֣יו עֲנָנָ֑ה יְ֝בַעֲתֻ֗הוּ כִּֽמְרִ֥ירֵי יֽוֹם׃

passages.text: If only darkness had taken that night away! May it not appear among the days of the year; may it never be entered in any of the months.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in deep sorrow.
He wishes for darkness to take that night away.
He does not want that night to be counted among the days of the year.
He does not want that night to be included in any of the months.
passages.original: הַלַּ֥יְלָה הַהוּא֮ יִקָּחֵ֪ה֫וּ אֹ֥פֶל אַל־ יִ֭חַדְּ בִּימֵ֣י שָׁנָ֑ה בְּמִסְפַּ֥ר יְ֝רָחִ֗ים אַל־ יָבֹֽא׃

passages.text: Behold, may that night be barren; may no joyful voice come into it.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in deep sorrow.
He refers to a specific night.
He says, “Behold, may that night be barren.”
He asks that no joyful voice enter that night.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֤ה הַלַּ֣יְלָה הַ֭הוּא יְהִ֣י גַלְמ֑וּד אַל־ תָּבֹ֖א רְנָנָ֣ה בֽוֹ׃

passages.text: May it be cursed by those who curse the day — those prepared to rouse Leviathan.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in deep sorrow.
He refers to people who curse days.
These people are ready to awaken Leviathan, a great sea creature.
Job asks these people to curse that night.
He wants that night to be removed and forgotten.
passages.original: יִקְּבֻ֥הוּ אֹרְרֵי־ י֑וֹם הָ֝עֲתִידִ֗ים עֹרֵ֥ר לִוְיָתָֽן׃

passages.text: May its morning stars grow dark; may it wait in vain for daylight; may it not see the breaking of dawn.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in deep sorrow.
He curses the night of his birth.
He says, "May its morning stars grow dark."
He means, "Let the stars that bring light to that night lose their brightness."
He says, "May it wait for daylight, but find none."
He means, "Let that night hope for morning, but let morning never come."
He says, "May it not see the breaking of dawn."
He means, "Let that night never witness the first light of day."
passages.original: יֶחְשְׁכוּ֮ כּוֹכְבֵ֪י נִ֫שְׁפּ֥וֹ יְקַו־ לְא֥וֹר וָאַ֑יִן וְאַל־ יִ֝רְאֶ֗ה בְּעַפְעַפֵּי־ שָֽׁחַר׃

passages.text: For that night did not shut the doors of the womb to hide the sorrow from my eyes.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in deep sorrow.
He wishes he had never been born.
He says the night of his birth did not close the doors of his mother’s womb.
The night allowed him to be born.
It did not hide trouble and pain from his eyes.
passages.original: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א סָ֭גַר דַּלְתֵ֣י בִטְנִ֑י וַיַּסְתֵּ֥ר עָ֝מָ֗ל מֵעֵינָֽי׃

passages.text: Why did I not perish at birth; why did I not die as I came from the womb?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in deep sorrow.
He asks a question about his own birth.
He says, “Why did I not die when I was born?”
He says, “Why did I not perish as I came out of my mother’s womb?”
passages.original: לָ֤מָּה לֹּ֣א מֵרֶ֣חֶם אָמ֑וּת מִבֶּ֖טֶן יָצָ֣אתִי וְאֶגְוָֽע׃

passages.text: Why were there knees to receive me, and breasts that I should be nursed?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in deep sorrow.
Job asks a question about his birth.
He says, “Why did someone hold me on their knees?”
He also says, “Why did someone nurse me at their breasts?”
Job wonders why anyone cared for him as a baby.
passages.original: מַ֭דּוּעַ קִדְּמ֣וּנִי בִרְכָּ֑יִם וּמַה־ שָּׁ֝דַ֗יִם כִּ֣י אִינָֽק׃

passages.text: For now I would be lying down in peace; I would be asleep and at rest with kings and counselors of the earth, who built for themselves cities now in ruins, or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in his suffering.
He wishes he had died at birth.
He says, “Now I would be lying down in peace.”
He would be asleep.
He would be at rest.
He would rest with kings of the earth.
He would rest with counselors of the earth.
These kings and counselors built cities for themselves.
Now those cities are in ruins.
He would also rest with princes.
These princes had much gold.
They filled their houses with silver.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ עַ֭תָּה שָׁכַ֣בְתִּי וְאֶשְׁק֑וֹט יָ֝שַׁ֗נְתִּי אָ֤ז׀ יָנ֬וּחַֽ לִֽי׃ עִם־ מְ֭לָכִים וְיֹ֣עֲצֵי אָ֑רֶץ הַבֹּנִ֖ים חֳרָב֣וֹת לָֽמוֹ׃ א֣וֹ עִם־ שָׂ֭רִים זָהָ֣ב לָהֶ֑ם הַֽמְמַלְאִ֖ים בָּתֵּיהֶ֣ם כָּֽסֶף׃

passages.text: Or why was I not hidden like a stillborn child, like an infant who never sees daylight?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in deep sorrow.
He wishes he had never lived.
He asks, "Why was I not hidden like a stillborn child?"
He says, "I could have been like an infant who never sees daylight."
He longs for rest from his suffering.
He desires to escape pain by never being born.
passages.original: א֤וֹ כְנֵ֣פֶל טָ֭מוּן לֹ֣א אֶהְיֶ֑ה כְּ֝עֹלְלִ֗ים לֹא־ רָ֥אוּ אֽוֹר׃

passages.text: There the wicked cease from raging, and there the weary find rest.
passages.sermon:
In that place, the wicked stop their anger.
In that place, the weary rest.
The wicked do not rage anymore.
The tired find peace.
passages.original: שָׁ֣ם רְ֭שָׁעִים חָ֣דְלוּ רֹ֑גֶז וְשָׁ֥ם יָ֝נ֗וּחוּ יְגִ֣יעֵי כֹֽחַ׃

passages.text: The captives enjoy their ease; they do not hear the voice of the oppressor.
passages.sermon: Captives are there.\r\nCaptives feel at ease.\r\nCaptives do not hear the oppressor’s voice.
passages.original: יַ֭חַד אֲסִירִ֣ים שַׁאֲנָ֑נוּ לֹ֥א שָׁ֝מְע֗וּ ק֣וֹל נֹגֵֽשׂ׃

passages.text: Both small and great are there, and the slave is freed from his master.
passages.sermon: In that place, both small people and great people are present.\r\nThe slave is free from his master.
passages.original: קָטֹ֣ן וְ֭גָדוֹל שָׁ֣ם ה֑וּא וְ֝עֶ֗בֶד חָפְשִׁ֥י מֵאֲדֹנָֽיו׃

passages.text: Why is light given to the miserable, and life to the bitter of soul, who long for death that does not come, and search for it like hidden treasure, who rejoice and greatly exult when they can find the grave?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks about people who suffer deeply.
These people feel miserable.
They have bitter souls.
God gives them light.
God gives them life.
These people long for death.
Death does not come to them.
They search for death like people search for hidden treasure.
They rejoice greatly when they find the grave.
passages.original: לָ֤מָּה יִתֵּ֣ן לְעָמֵ֣ל א֑וֹר וְ֝חַיִּ֗ים לְמָ֣רֵי נָֽפֶשׁ׃ הַֽמְחַכִּ֣ים לַמָּ֣וֶת וְאֵינֶ֑נּוּ וַֽ֝יַּחְפְּרֻ֗הוּ מִמַּטְמוֹנִֽים׃ הַשְּׂמֵחִ֥ים אֱלֵי־ גִ֑יל יָ֝שִׂ֗ישׂוּ כִּ֣י יִמְצְאוּ־ קָֽבֶר׃

passages.text: Why is life given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks about a man.
This man cannot see his path.
God has hidden the way from him.
God has placed barriers around him.
This man still receives life.
Job asks why God gives life to such a man.
passages.original: לְ֭גֶבֶר אֲשֶׁר־ דַּרְכּ֣וֹ נִסְתָּ֑רָה וַיָּ֖סֶךְ אֱל֣וֹהַּ בַּעֲדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: I sigh when food is put before me, and my groans pour out like water.
passages.sermon:
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
He feels deep sorrow.
He sighs when he sees his food.
His groans pour out like water.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ לִפְנֵ֣י לַ֭חְמִי אַנְחָתִ֣י תָבֹ֑א וַֽיִּתְּכ֥וּ כַ֝מַּ֗יִם שַׁאֲגֹתָֽי׃

passages.text: For the thing I feared has overtaken me, and what I dreaded has befallen me.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks about his suffering.
He says he feared something bad would happen.
That fear has now come true.
What he dreaded has happened to him.
His worst fears have become real.
passages.original: כִּ֤י פַ֣חַד פָּ֭חַדְתִּי וַיֶּאֱתָיֵ֑נִי וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָ֝גֹ֗רְתִּי יָ֣בֹא לִֽי׃

passages.text: I am not at ease or quiet; I have no rest, for trouble has come.”
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is suffering greatly.
Job says, “I am not at ease.
I am not quiet.
I have no rest.
Trouble has come to me.”
passages.original: לֹ֤א שָׁלַ֨וְתִּי׀ וְלֹ֖א שָׁקַ֥טְתִּי וְֽלֹא־ נָ֗חְתִּי וַיָּ֥בֹא רֹֽגֶז׃פ
